title: Immunization Record Standard: Posting a Store-Given Dose to the Course Record (Immunization Services)
content:
# Immunization Services — posting a dose given at a Kestrel store

**Record standard.** When a dose a Kestrel pharmacist gave today did not reach the record, the desk posts it, and the posted dose takes the dose number of the series that Kestrel's record conventions give it.

## 1. Consent that covers a posted dose

1.1 A dose posted after the visit is covered by the screening and consent form signed for the appointment it was given at no more than the consent validity days before, counted in calendar days with the signing date as day 0, whatever dose number the appointment and the form print; the form is signed by the patient, or below the guardian-consent age by a parent or guardian, and never by Kestrel staff for them.

1.2 A dose given and recorded at the visit itself is given only when a screening and consent form for that dose was signed no more than the consent validity days before, counted in calendar days with the signing date as day 0.

The consent validity days and the guardian-consent age are the vaccination's own figures in the Immunization Services product tables.

| Question the record answers | Dose posted after the visit | Dose given and recorded at the visit |
|---|---|---|
| Which form covers the dose | The form signed for the appointment the dose was given at | A form signed for that dose |
| Does the dose number printed on the appointment or form matter | No — the form covers the dose whatever number it prints | The form is for that dose |
| How recent the form must be | Signed no more than the consent validity days before, signing date as day 0 | Signed no more than the consent validity days before, signing date as day 0 |
| Who may sign | The patient, or below the guardian-consent age a parent or guardian; never Kestrel staff | — |

*Boundary illustration.* Counting the signing date as day 0, a form still covers a dose given on the day whose count equals the consent validity days, and no longer covers a dose given on the day after it.

## 2. What a posting puts on the record

A posting adds one dose-given entry, dated today, to the course history, tied to the kept appointment. The entry records the store, the dose number, the lot number, how the dose is paid, the insurance plan billed if any, whether the dose completes the course, and the observation minutes. The amount the patient pays is left open on the entry. The posting takes one dose off the course's valid doses still needed; a dose that completes the course closes it as completed today, and the first dose of a longer series marks the course in progress. After the posting, the course history carries the dose as a given dose with its observation minutes recorded and its payment still open.

## 3. How the action is invoked

The action is the agent-side tool `post_missed_dose_006fe732`. It is unlocked and then called by the agent; it is not handed over to the patient.

## 4. Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `course_id` | Reference number of the vaccination course the dose belongs to, as returned by the course lookup | Id |
| `source_event_id` | Reference number of the booked appointment the dose was given at, as returned by the vaccination history lookup | Id |
| `store_id` | Reference number of the Kestrel store where the dose was given, as returned by the store lookup or the appointment | Id |
| `dose_number` | The dose of the course that was given | Positive integer dose number |
| `lot_number` | The vaccine lot number printed on the patient's vaccination record card | Verbatim — copied character for character as the patient reads it out |
| `billing_route` | How the dose is paid | One of the four values below |
| `coverage_id` | Reference number of the insurance plan billed for the dose, as returned by the insurance plan lookup | Id; pass "" for a cash or Vaccines for Children dose |
| `is_final_dose` | Whether this dose completes the course | true when it brings the course's valid doses to the doses required; false when more doses remain |
| `observation_minutes` | Minutes the patient is recorded as observed after the dose | Integer minutes |

Values of `billing_route`:

- `medical_benefit` — billed to Medicare Part B;
- `pharmacy_benefit` — billed to a prescription insurance plan;
- `cash` — the patient pays the cash price;
- `no_cost_program` — given from Vaccines for Children stock.

## 5. Return

A successful call returns `dose_record_id` (reference number of the posted dose entry), `course_id`, `dose_number`, `event_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD), `observation_minutes`, `doses_remaining` (the course's valid doses still needed after the dose) and `course_status`. A returned `dose_record_id` means the dose is on the record.
